protocol.description:
This protocol lets a compositor grant future presentation opportunities and lets an ordinary wl_surface target exactly one granted opportunity.
Epoch and sequence form the immutable identity. Timestamps are scheduling estimates in the compositor's wp_presentation clock domain and must not be used to recover or relabel identity. A targeted commit is latched for its named opportunity only if it is ready by then. A commit that misses it is never discarded or relabelled onto a later grant: it applies untargeted once ready and is shown at the next opportunity, and its buffer is released like any other.

interface.name: denial_frame_timeline_manager_v1
interface.description: The global is optional. Clients requiring exact presentation must fail closed when it is absent rather than synthesize another clock.

request.name: get_timeline
request.description: The new timeline starts disarmed. set_active controls grant delivery.

request.name: get_surface_timeline

description.summary: add exact targeting to an ordinary surface

request.description: Creating this object does not alter the surface's role, input routing, scene ownership, or presentation-feedback behavior.

entry.name: invalid_active
entry.summary: active is neither zero nor one

request.name: set_active
request.description: Disarming aborts all grants not yet latched. Re-arming begins with the current epoch and future opportunities; grants are never replayed.

arg.name: active
arg.summary: zero to disarm, one to arm

event.name: grant
event.description: latch_* is the last compositor scheduling boundary at which a ready targeted commit can be accepted. target_* is the predicted physical presentation time. period_ns is the nominal refresh period.

event.name: epoch

description.summary: invalidate all identities from prior epochs

event.description: This event is sent before any grant in the named epoch. Clients must abort queued work from every other epoch.

interface.name: denial_surface_frame_timeline_v1

description.summary: exact target for an ordinary wl_surface commit

interface.description: set_target is double-buffered surface state and applies to the next wl_surface.commit. It is consumed by that commit. An expired, unissued, inactive-epoch, or regressing target leaves that commit untargeted; it does not disconnect the client. Cross-client object references remain protocol errors.

entry.name: target_regression
entry.summary: target is not newer than prior target

request.name: set_target
request.description: The target is a scheduling constraint, not a client-liveness contract. A commit is latched for its grant only at the named latch; a late commit counts as a miss for that grant and is never relabelled onto a later one or burst to catch up. Semantic scheduling misses never disconnect the client.
